description: Open an http(s) URL in the current tab. Returns evidence and a snapshot of the visible screen (elements carry refs like e12), with counts of what is above and below; snapshot:false returns the start of the page's text instead, for a page you will read or leave (browser_get_text reads on from where it stops). Words like cheapest, latest, highest-rated or most mean the site's own sort or tab for that order (a list's default order is usually something else, e.g. 'Best' or 'Featured'): open that tab or choose that sort (a label naming its best value is not the list), read the top, and say in the answer which sort, tab and filters it came from. The top is the answer only when that order ranks by what the task asks over everything inside its bounds; otherwise say how much was read and call the pick the best of those read, not the best. Break a tie in that order only by what the task asks; otherwise report the tie. Search, sort and filter addresses: you may build one from the task's own words (a query, a place, dates, a sort, a bound) or change a parameter this site has shown you in an address or link (browser_query gives a link's full href), its page number included. A search the site's form takes several steps for (a place, dates, guests, a sort, filters) is usually one call as such an address, where the form takes a call and a screen for each step. Before you use its results, check on the page that what you meant was applied: the heading, breadcrumb, selected sort or filter, and the results themselves (each one you count inside the bound); never the address or a search box, which can repeat a value the site ignored. When they do not match or a bound cannot be checked, use the site's own form, or say in the answer what could not be applied. Never write a sign-in, session, account, identity or tracking value yourself (tokens, ids, codes): keep one only as the site gave it, or leave it out. Over several sites, finish one and note the values the next needs before opening it. A task that names no site: search the web first with browser_search, not a search engine's own page, to pick the site, or answer from the search when that is enough; when search engines show a bot check, search inside a site that answers (its search box, or a search address it has shown you) rather than guessing addresses; open a site when the task needs one (a price for dates, a form, an account).

snapshot.description: Default true. Choose by your next step on this page: false returns the start of the page's readable text in place of the screen (no refs), for a page you will read or leave; keep true when you will click, type or choose on it (you need its refs). Both say where it landed, the title, loading notes and anything that needs a person; browser_snapshot shows the screen at any time.
